query: Consider the following context: The ability to endure extreme corrosion in challenging environments is reduced in stainless steel. This can be addressed by appropriate surface modification techniques to redefine the surface with the required properties. In that context, which method can be used for improved corrosion resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A computationally guided surface modification based on DFT‐optimized passivating chemistries, applied as an ultrathin coating via a precise deposition technique such as ALD, will significantly improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme, aggressive environments compared to its untreated state.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk stainless steel with its conventional passive film that is insufficient to resist extreme corrosive conditions.
generation.intervention: Deposit an ultrathin, DFT‐derived passivating film (using, for example, atomic layer deposition) onto the stainless steel surface.
generation.conditions: Exposure to extreme corrosive environments (e.g., high chloride concentration environments or molten salt conditions) where conventional stainless steel shows high corrosion rates.
generation.structural_mediator: The tailored coating modifies the surface chemistry by introducing a more noble, densely packed passivating layer that limits micro-galvanic activity and aggressive electrochemical reactions.
generation.mechanism: DFT calculations identify alloying elements and optimal surface compositions that increase the electrochemical stability of the surface, thereby reducing localized corrosion initiated by environmental aggressors.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable decrease in corrosion rate (e.g., reduced weight loss and altered electrochemical profiles) compared to untreated stainless steel under identical harsh environmental conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated stainless steel exhibiting its standard, less effective passive film in extreme corrosive environments.
generation.boundary: The improvement is contingent on achieving a uniform, defect-free, and durable coating; under conditions where the film is compromised mechanically or by thermal cycling, the benefit may be reduced.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of corrosion resistance improvement and the long-term stability of the coating under cyclic or mechanically challenging conditions remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of stainless steel samples: one set coated with the DFT-optimized passivating film using ALD and an untreated control set. Subject both sets to a standardized extreme corrosive environment (e.g., high chloride solution or molten salt at elevated temperature) for a predetermined duration.
measurements: Corrosion rate via weight loss measurements
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) to assess barrier properties
Surface analysis (SEM/EDS) to evaluate coating integrity and signs of degradation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DFT-optimized coated samples do not show a statistically significant reduction in corrosion rate and improved electrochemical stability over the untreated samples, the hypothesis will be falsified.
